spam.heading: Open to everyone. Closed to bots.
spam.subheading: Letting anyone post without an account raises an obvious question. Here's the answer: every submission is scored before it publishes, and your users never see a CAPTCHA.
spam.scoredDesc: Link stuffing, disposable inboxes, duplicate text and floods from one source are all weighted before anything reaches your board.
spam.quarantineDesc: High-confidence spam never appears publicly. Nothing is destroyed — it waits in a review queue with the reason it was caught.
spam.restoreDesc: Anything caught by mistake goes straight back to the board, and stops being flagged again.

faq.heading: Questions people ask before signing up
faq.spamQ: Won't anonymous posting fill my board with spam?
faq.spamA: That's the first thing everyone asks. Every submission is scored before it publishes — link stuffing, disposable email domains, duplicate text and bursts from a single source all count against it. Obvious spam is quarantined and never appears publicly. Anything borderline is published but flagged for you, with the reason it was caught, and one click restores it. Your users never see a CAPTCHA.
faq.signinQ: Can I require people to sign in anyway?
faq.signinA: Yes. It's a single switch in Branding settings on Pro and above. It's off by default because open feedback is the point of the product, but if you need accounts, you can have them — and you can always turn it back off, on any plan.
faq.freeA: One workspace, a public board, roadmap and changelog, unlimited posts and votes, and up to two team members. There's no cap on how much feedback you can collect and no time limit. Paid plans add attachments, contacting submitters, a verified owner badge, more seats and more workspaces.
faq.domainQ: Can I use my own branding and domain?
faq.domainA: Your board lives on your own subdomain with your logo and brand colour on every plan. A fully custom domain is available on paid plans. Tenant boards carry no FeedBoard advertising of any kind.
faq.exportA: Yes. Your feedback, roadmap and changelog belong to you, and there's a REST API to read it all out. Deleting your account removes the workspaces you own along with their contents — no lock-in and no hostage-taking.
faq.afterQ: What happens right after I sign up?
faq.afterA: You name your workspace, pick a subdomain, and you're on your board — about three minutes, no credit card. The next step is sharing the link with your users, which is the only thing standing between you and your first piece of real feedback.
